project.description: The project this object belongs to.

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

operations.description:
{@link MlModel} operations to run on the {@link MlModel.Route} selected by {@link #routeFilter}.
Route job supports the following operations on {@link MlModel}: train, score, process, and interpret only.
key is the name of operation, and the value is the {@link MlModel.Input} to use for the operation.

NOTE: Keys are case-sensitive and is one of "train", "process", "score" or "interpret" only as defined in {@link MlDataOpName}.
NOTE: "train" operation, if specified, will always precede, and the resultant trained model will be used by "score", "process", and "interpret" operations.
NOTE: unless specified by {@link MlModel.Route.OperationJobSpec#doNotHandleOutputs}, the outputs of the "process"
  and "interpret" operations will be handled by the output handlers configured on the route.
NOTE: the `subjectFilter` field of `MlModel.Input` will be ignored and replaced by {@link MlModel.Route#subjectFilter}
  of the route for which the operations are run.

title:
Represents a job for running (possibly multiple) operations on many {@link MlModel.Route}s. All {@link MlModel.Route}s
should be within the scope of a single {@link MlProject}.
See {@link #routeFilter} and {@link #operations} for how to define the routes and operations to run, respectively.
Each route's {@link MlModel} will have the specified operation(s) performed on it, with results persisted as a
{@link MlModel.Route.OperationJob.Result}.
Since this is a route-based job, all operations will be "global", i.e. executed on the entire subject segment
described by the route's subject filter unbatched. If this is an issue for any of your operations, then it is
recommended to use {@link MlSubject.OperationJob} instead, which will batch the subjects for your operation.

Usage:
Simple prediction
```python
route_op_job = c3.MlModel.Route.OperationJob(
    project=project,
    operations={
        c3.MlDataOpName.PROCESS: c3.MlModel.Input(start="01-01-2023", end="01-08-2023")
    }
).create()
job_run = route_op_job.start(routeFilter="status.label=='CHAMPION'")
```

Retrain underlying pipeline prior to each prediction, i.e. "One-shot" train/predict
```python
route_op_job = c3.MlModel.Route.OperationJob(
    project=project,
    operations={
        c3.MlDataOpName.TRAIN: c3.MlModel.Input(start="01-01-2022", end="01-01-2023"),
        c3.MlDataOpName.SCORE: c3.MlModel.Input(start="01-01-2022", end="01-01-2023"),
        c3.MlDataOpName.PROCESS: c3.MlModel.Input(start="01-01-2023", end="01-08-2023")
    }
).create()
job_run = route_op_job.start(routeFilter="status.label=='CHAMPION'")
```
name: MlModel.Route.OperationJob
